https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/.text: The Polish prime minister’s office has confirmed the planned meeting between Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. "This afternoon in Lublin, Prime Minister Donald Tusk will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The topic of the talks will be a summary of his visit to the United States and the meeting with President Donald Trump," the PM’s office said on X on Wednesday.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Police officers at Leipzig airport search for a drone that may be connected to a suspected attack on 7 August. Photograph: Sebastian Willnow/DPA/AP View image in fullscreen Police officers at Leipzig airport search for a drone that may be connected to a suspected attack on 7 August. Photograph: Sebastian Willnow/DPA/AP Germany Germany poised to identify suspect in Leipzig drone attack on Ukrainian plane Berlin expected to outline response to incident this month widely speculated to have been coordinated by Russia Kate Connolly in Berlin Mon 31 Aug 2026 10.14 EDT Last modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 10.25 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The German government is imminently expected to announce who it believes was behind a suspected drone attack on a Ukrainian cargo plane earlier this month and to outline its response to the incident in coordination with its European and Nato partners. The chancellor, Friedrich Merz, told the public broadcaster ARD in an interview on Sunday evening: “We are in the process of concluding the investigations; we have reached a broad agreement within the federal government on how we will respond, and we will make this clear in the coming days. It won’t take much longer.” The government has so far declined to say officially who it thinks was behind the attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle airport on 4 August. There has been widespread speculation that it was coordinated by Moscow. A drone containing explosives was discovered near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft used to transport military supplies. The drone was apparently intended to land on the wings of the aircraft, which was filled with kerosene, but the explosive device did not detonate, according to a report last week referencing the investigation. About 20 minutes after the discovery of the first drone, a second drone possibly collided with a DHL cargo plane, which had to abort its landing manoeuvre and was diverted. Days later, a third drone was found in a field in a municipality that directly borders the western edge of Leipzig airport. Forensic technicians from the federal criminal police office found residues of a substance that initial assessments indicated could have been the highly explosive substance hexogen. This explosive also failed to detonate but according to media reports, the investigators’ report stated: “The perpetrators may have had a far larger attack in mind than previously known to the public.” Moscow has denied involvement. The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe Read more Merz indicated that the information the government was due to release was being closely communicated with Berlin’s partners, and any response would also be carried out in cooperation with them. “It will be a response from Germany , but our partners in the European Union and Nato will not be taken by surprise,” he said. It has been speculated in Berlin that meetings this week of EU defence and foreign affairs ministers in Wicklow, Ireland, could be used to make the announcement. Last week Merz stopped short of naming a suspect but said: “They will pay for this.” He underscored the necessity for a decisive response due to the lengths he said those behind the Leipzig plot and other acts of sabotage had been prepared to go. “Attackers are increasingly ruthlessly accepting even serious property damage, and even injuries and deaths,” he said. The daily Die Welt and the news website Politico have reported, citing sources, that the government will blame Russia for the attack and that its retaliatory measures are likely to include a new, extensive package of sanctions coordinated with Brussels to hinder it financially, as well as more forceful measures against Russia’s shadow fleet, the Russian ships illegally transporting oil. The closure of Russian House, an institution representing Russia’s cultural interests that has a large presence in the centre of Berlin, is also said to be on the cards. In return, Russia would be expected to close Germany’s cultural body in Russia, the Goethe Institute. The political dimensions of the government’s response are potentially considerable owing to the timing. A heated election campaign in eastern German states culminates in a vote this Sunday in which the anti-immigrant, populist AfD is expected to do well. The debate over relations with Russia and whether and how Germany should continue to support Ukraine are playing an important role in the campaign. The AfD’s foreign policy spokesperson, Markus Frohnmaier, said he believed “without a doubt” Germany faced hybrid threats but said he would not speculate over who was behind them, calling on the government to “first establish transparency and provide information about the current state of knowledge”. https://baltic-review.com/riga-survival-.text: Share Tweet 0 Survival Kit 17 will use Riga Congress Hall as its main venue from 28 August to 27 September 2026. Riga’s Survival Kit contemporary art festival is preparing to open its seventeenth edition with a programme centred on care, healing and the ways people create knowledge together. The festival will run from 28 August to 27 September 2026 at Riga Congress Hall, with a preview programme beginning on 27 August. The announcement gives Latvia’s late-summer cultural calendar a distinctly social emphasis. Rather than presenting contemporary art only as a collection of objects, Survival Kit 17 will combine an exhibition with performances, conversations, mediated walks and guided tours. Its organisers describe the central theme as “care”, while the full title — “Wind Arrow: On Art and Healing” — points towards art as a space for reflection, exchange and shared attention. A festival built around participation The edition is curated by Elena Sorokina and Simona Markela Dvorák in collaboration with the Initiative for Practices and Visions of Radical Care. According to the programme announcement published by Riga’s municipal culture department, the curatorial approach examines the overlapping territory between artistic work and healing practices. That focus will be visible from the opening evening. On 27 August, three performances will be presented at Riga Congress Hall in cooperation with the Centre Pompidou in Paris. The programme is scheduled to include work by musician and composer Naima Nefertari, choreographer Zora Snake and artist Maya Minder. The projects connect performance with ritual, sensory experience, food, fermentation and the transmission of knowledge. The opening will continue at Kaņepes Culture Centre with a “Healing Nightclub”, an interdisciplinary evening combining sound, music and dance. The programme is intended less as a conventional concert than as a shared experiment in how audiences experience art through the body and through collective presence. From movement practices to public discussion The festival’s public programme extends beyond the opening weekend. On 28 August, artist Zaiga Putrāma will lead a movement practice based on principles of tango communication. The event is presented as an invitation to explore interaction, listening and non-verbal exchange. Survival Kit 17 will also take part in Riga’s White Night programme on 5 September. The evening will include T.I.E.’s performance “Veins of Daugava / Uterine Waters”, which treats water as a space of memory, transformation and continuity. The Daugava will serve as a symbolic and sonic axis, connecting local cultural references with diasporic practices. Another White Night project, “Appendix — A Cut into the Side Layers”, will address questions of coexistence, belonging and inclusion in Latvia. The project will involve a movement performance by Latvian artists and women from third countries living in Latvia, followed by a public discussion led by artist Viktoria Fomenko. Later in September, writer Agnese Krivade will lead a guided presence practice inspired by the publication “Entangled Landscapes: Navigation”. The event, titled “A Walk in an Ugly Landscape”, is planned for 12 September. On 17 September, a discussion moderated by associate professor and media theorist Ilva Skulte will examine art education as a form of care, including questions of value, sustainability and institutional change. Making contemporary art more accessible A notable part of the programme is the role assigned to art mediators. On Thursday and Friday evenings, specially trained mediators supported by the VV Foundation will be present in the exhibition to encourage conversation between visitors and works on display. The organisers are also offering mediator-led individual and group tours, as well as visits for schools. This approach places interpretation and discussion at the centre of the visitor experience, potentially making the exhibition more welcoming to people who may not regularly attend contemporary art events. Survival Kit has been organised by the Latvian Centre for Contemporary Art since 2009. The festival is known for using vacant or underused buildings as exhibition venues, turning questions about urban space and public access into part of the artistic experience. This year’s main venue, Riga Congress Hall, will host the exhibition from 28 August through 27 September. Practical information The exhibition will be open from Tuesday to Saturday between 12:00 and 20:00, and on Sundays from 12:00 to 18:00. It will be closed on Mondays. Standard admission is €8, with a €5 ticket available to students and seniors. Admission is free for preschool children, school pupils, art-school students, people with disabilities and their accompanying persons. Families holding a 3+ Family Card can also purchase a €5 family ticket. By linking exhibition visits with performances, guided encounters and public debate, Survival Kit 17 presents contemporary art as part of civic and social life in Riga. Its programme does not promise a single answer to the pressures of contemporary life. Instead, it offers a month-long setting in which visitors can consider how attention, knowledge, movement and hospitality might become shared forms of care. https://www.politico.eu/article/france-p.text: PARIS — French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Wednesday pledged to address protesting high school students’ concerns while also announcing the release of strategic fuel reserves to lower prices. "The anger among young people didn't come out of nowhere," Lecornu said as he addressed the nation. The center-right prime minister said his government’s first policy responses to protesters’ concerns — including run-down schools, a shortage of substitute teachers, and a desire for more manageable schedules — would come later this month. The government will consider submissions on a public platform set up Tuesday to allow students to voice their grievances. Advertisement Advertisement On Tuesday, between 256,000 people, according to police, and 450,000, according to organizers, joined demonstrations across France. Unions, teachers and left-wing political parties took to the streets in solidarity with high school students. But discontent in France extends beyond schools. A surge in fuel prices, triggered by the U.S.-led war in Iran, has added to concerns about the cost of living. Online calls for a Yellow Jackets -style protest on Oct. 17 have emerged in response to rising fuel prices. "Last Friday, [the G7] decided to release strategic [fuel] reserves... As part of this effort, we will make 10 million barrels of diesel from our reserves available to distributors in France," Lecornu announced, claiming that the supply increase would lower diesel prices by €0.12 to €0.18 per liter. France still has 8 million barrels of oil products to release under a wider deal brokered in March after the outbreak of the war in Iran, and had privately signaled Wednesday morning that it might release an additional 2 million barrels of diesel on top of that, as POLITICO reported earlier on Wednesday . It's unclear whether the 10 million figure includes that earlier commitment. The French energy ministry did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Advertisement Advertisement Lecornu also reached out to French farmers, who have regularly protested in recent years to draw attention to the sector’s economic hardships. “Among those hardest hit by the accumulation of these crises are our farmers,” Lecornu said. He said new measures to supplement an emergency bill for farmers, which already includes more than €1 billion in spending , would be unveiled Thursday. Nicolas Camut contributed to this report.
